title: One smooth dimension cut preserving a connected finite étale cover
statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field, X a connected affine k-scheme, and f : X → Spec k smooth of constant relative dimension d ≥ 2. Let π : T → X be a finite étale morphism with T connected. Let S be a nonempty finite set of k-rational points of X, represented by sections s : Spec k → X of f. There exist a scheme Y and a closed immersion j : Y → X such that Y is affine and connected, j followed by f is smooth of relative dimension d−1, every s in S factors through j, and T ×_X Y is connected. Scheme, smoothness, closed immersion, finiteness, étaleness and affineness use [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; fibre products use [def-pc-base-change]. No descent or iteration to dimension one is asserted.

source.place: Paragraphs 2–4, up to construction of X₁

proof.text: Put the specified structure map f into X.Over. Smooth connected X is regular and locally Noetherian, hence irreducible. The proved smooth-relative-dimension dimension formula and irreducibleComponents_eq_singleton give pure dimension d. Form F as the finite image of the unique point of each section. The rational-point/closed-point equivalence proves its points closed.

Apply the affine coordinate smooth-system interface to F. It supplies the invertible module L, the coefficient group Fin r → k, an additive map with the canonical scalar identity, vanishing on F, generation and immersion off F, and a nonempty smooth affine pure-dimensional-member coefficient open O.

Apply the existing finite-cover irreducible-system theorem to exactly this basis Pi.basisFun and section map. It supplies the second nonempty coefficient open P. The polynomial spectrum is irreducible, so O ∩ P is nonempty. It is Jacobson; choose a closed point, use pointOfClosedPoint to obtain a k-point, and express its ring map as evaluation at the images of the variables. This proves that one coefficient tuple lies in both opens.

The chosen member is smooth, affine, pure of dimension d-1, and connected, and its finite-cover pullback is connected. Smooth connectedness gives irreducibility; the component definition of pure dimension gives its total dimension. The proved smoothOfRelativeDimension_iff_topologicalKrullDim_eq therefore gives relative dimension d-1. Vanishing puts each rational section point in the support, equal to the range of the closed immersion; IsClosedImmersion.existsUnique_fac_of_field supplies the required factorization.

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 2–4; K4 implements rational coefficient selection, the finite-cover application, point factorization and dimension conversion. The projective-closure and basis-coordinate smooth-system conversion is isolated separately.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_smooth_finiteCover_dimension_cut {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsAffine X] [ConnectedSpace X]
    {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (π : T ⟶ X) [IsFinite π] [Etale π] [ConnectedSpace T]
    (S : Finset (Spec (.of k) ⟶ X)) (hS : S.Nonempty)
    (hS' : ∀ s ∈ S, s ≫ f = 𝟙 _) :
    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (j : Y ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion j ∧ IsAffine Y ∧
      SmoothOfRelativeDimension (d - 1) (j ≫ f) ∧ ConnectedSpace Y ∧
      (∀ s ∈ S, ∃ t, t ≫ j = s) ∧ ConnectedSpace ↑(pullback π j)
